results.judged_by: automatic rule per ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1 as the card instantiates it: survived = overall TPR inside the original's 95% CI AND at least 20 pp below the expert majority vote (99.3) AND the evasion blocks at least 20 pp below the clean blocks AND FPR <= 20; partial = level or FPR moves while the gradient holds; dead = the gradient disappears; human double-coding pending
results.note: TPR 55.33 [47.3, 63.1] (83/150) vs paper 54.0; FPR 4.00 [1.8, 8.5] (6/150) vs paper 4.0; evasion gradient 50.0 pp; unparsed 0

reproducibility_frictions_observed: the released record's own 'id' field is not unique (61 distinct values for 150 articles); items are keyed on the dict index '0'-'299' instead - the Tier B run mis-paired 89 replies before the responses were re-matched by request hash

models.Detector.__init__ opens the prompt files by relative path and without an encoding: the adapter chdirs into the repository and defaults open() to UTF-8, without which prompts/detection_guide.txt raises UnicodeDecodeError on a non-UTF-8 locale
models.py imports torch, transformers and anthropic at module level although the OpenAI detector path uses none of them (~25 s import)
the repository ships no scoring script: TPR/FPR aggregation per Table 2 block is ours
the release gold strings are 'AI-generated' / 'Human-written'; the README example and the Tier B config say 'Machine-generated'

helpers.model_call in the same repository hard-codes reasoning_effort='high' for o1, contradicting footnote 22; that path is not the detector path and models.py sends no reasoning_effort at all (API default 'medium')
a reply without an <answer> tag yields None in the authors' parser; such a reply is not a label and is reported separately, not folded into HUMAN-WRITTEN (the Tier B runner folded it)
